question: How does the mātṛkā wheel awaken in the disciple?
premises: The mātṛkā-wheel awakening of the disciple is the remainder.
The supreme principle is supreme light alone, intolerant of fixed designations.
From freedom, wishing to manifest the universe, it manifests Śiva-Śakti-formness in itself.
The unfailing Śiva-characterized principle has full I-ness as its Śakti.
The letters from a to ha arise as powers, elements, senses, and principles.
The universe is known as expressed-expressor, six-course, resting in the unsurpassed.
The guru marked by knowing beginningless-endless I-reflection is worshipable and grants accomplishment.
inference: Thus the disciple's awakening is full recognition of the supreme principle as I-ness, through which the mātṛkā letters and powers are known as manifestations of Śiva-Śakti.

plain_english: The awakening of the mātṛkā wheel in the disciple is the full recognition of the supreme principle as I-ness, through which the letters and powers of the universe are known as manifestations of Śiva and Śakti; the guru who knows this beginningless and endless I-reflection is worshipable and grants accomplishment.
